artifact.summary: Implements only the standard bit-flip query oracle O_f|x>|b> = |x>|b XOR f(x)> (eq_5) for an explicit truth table of f on n bits (1 <= n <= 11). Each input x with f(x)=1 gets a multi-controlled X onto the answer qubit, with X gates conjugating the zero-valued bits of x. The monotonicity tester itself is not reconstructed, because the abstract does not specify it.
register_layout: qubit 0: x_0 (least significant bit of query point x)
qubit 1..n-1: x_1..x_{n-1} (for the example n=2, qubit 1 is x_1, the most significant bit)
qubit n: b, answer qubit (index 2 in the example), receives b XOR f(x)
computational basis: |x>|b> with x = sum_i x_i 2^i; truth_table[x] = f(x)

equation_mapping.explanation: Definition of monotonicity. It defines the property being tested and is not part of the oracle circuit. The oracle accepts any truth table, monotone or not.
Definition of epsilon-farness via normalized Hamming distance. It is not needed to build the oracle.
The accept/reject guarantee belongs to the full tester, which the abstract does not specify and which is not reconstructed.
The query complexity bound concerns the unspecified algorithm. The circuit contains a single oracle application and no tester.

equation_mapping.code_location: build_circuit: loop over x with f(x)=1 applying X-conjugated multi-controlled X onto qubit n
equation_mapping.explanation: Implements O_f|x>|b> = |x>|b xor f(x)> from an explicit truth table, as a product of multi-controlled X gates. The control pattern for each x is selected by conjugating its zero bits with X.

specification_changes.change: The label 'Phase query oracle' conflicts with the formula, which is a bit-flip (standard XOR) oracle. The circuit implements the formula as written. A phase oracle could be obtained with b in |->.
specification_changes.reason: The formula is unambiguous, so it takes precedence over the label.

specification_changes.change: Scope narrowed to the oracle construction only. No tester, quantum search, or amplitude amplification is implemented.
specification_changes.reason: The abstract gives no algorithmic details, so any tester would be fabricated.

specification_changes.change: The function f is supplied as an explicit truth table, with n limited to 1..11.
specification_changes.reason: A circuit needs a concrete f, and the 12-qubit cap leaves n+1 <= 12.

assumptions: Little-endian encoding: bit i of the integer x is on qubit i.
The answer qubit is the single qubit with index n, after the n input qubits.
truth_table[x] = f(x) with entries 0 or 1 (booleans accepted).
Multi-controlled X is built with qc.mcx without ancillas and left for the transpiler to decompose.
unresolved_issues: The actual monotonicity-testing algorithm is not specified in the abstract and is not implemented.
The polylog factors hidden by the tilde in the query bound are unspecified.
The circuit contains no tester, so eq_3 and eq_4 cannot be checked against this module.

validation.detail: Circuit built and transpiled successfully; no independent correctness reference selected.
